headline: Margins widen and EPS climbs despite flat sales
summary_short: Core & Main's fiscal Q1 2026 (three months ended May 3, 2026) net sales were essentially flat y/y at $1,910M as volume declines in pipes/valves/fittings and storm drainage were offset by acquisitions, while gross margin rose 50bps to 27.2% and diluted EPS grew 9.6% to $0.57.
summary_long: Net sales were essentially flat y/y at $1,910M: volume declines in pipes/valves/fittings and storm drainage were offset by acquisitions, while fire protection and smart utility products grew on higher volume. Gross margin rose 50bps to 27.2% on gross-margin initiatives and disciplined pricing; SG&A rose 2.0% to $299M on distribution costs and growth investment. Operating income grew 3.5% to $177M, net income grew 8.0% to $108M on higher operating income and lower interest expense, and diluted EPS grew 9.6% to $0.57 on buybacks. No forward guidance was given. Cash ended at $150M after $88M of share repurchases and $42M of Tax Receivable Agreement payments; no dividend was declared.

drivers.explanation: Net sales were essentially flat as decreased volume in pipes/valves/fittings and storm drainage was offset by acquisitions; fire protection net sales rose on higher volume and pricing, and smart utility products rose on higher volume.
Gross profit and its margin ratio (27.2% vs 26.7%) rose primarily on favorable execution of gross-margin initiatives and disciplined purchasing and pricing management.
Same underlying driver as gross profit: favorable execution of gross-margin initiatives and disciplined purchasing and pricing management, per the release.
Operating income rose as higher gross profit was partially offset by higher SG&A (+2.0% to $299M) from higher distribution costs and growth investments, partly offset by recent cost-action benefits.

The release attributes its (differently-defined) Adjusted EBITDA increase to higher gross profit partially offset by higher SG&A; this shard's EBITDA figure uses a different basis but reflects the same dynamics.
Net income rose on higher operating income and lower interest expense ($27M vs $30M), from lower rates and reduced Senior ABL Credit Facility borrowings.
Basic EPS grew faster than net income because Class A weighted-average shares fell to 188.4M from 189.8M following share-repurchase transactions.
Diluted EPS grew faster than net income as diluted weighted-average shares fell to 195.7M from 198.7M following share-repurchase transactions.

MD&A frames the quarter as essentially flat net sales with margin expansion from gross-margin initiatives and pricing discipline, driving high-single-digit EPS growth despite soft volumes and no explicit forward guidance.
